subject: MAP: Post-signature phased acceptance & evaluation tie-offs - NovaGrid
content:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@novagrid.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Post-signature phased acceptance & evaluation tie-offs - NovaGrid

Elaine —

Congrats again on the signature. Attached is the first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation milestones we discussed: staged rollout, canary windows, migration cutovers, and training timelines. High-level asks from our side: a single technical point-of-contact for cutover approvals, confirmation on the acceptance criteria for the initial canary (latency p95 < 450ms for 99% of traffic, accuracy checks on 5 canonical prompt sets), and procurement target for the PO.

Key dates (draft):
- Week 0 (Nov 23): Kickoff + environment provisioning
- Week 1–2: Canary wave 1 (10% traffic) + evaluation runbook
- Week 3: Canary wave 2 (50% traffic) + training sessions for ops
- Week 4: Full migration + acceptance

I put you as primary external contact on the MAP. Please let us know if procurement prefers a single consolidated acceptance artifact or phased signoffs per canary wave.

Attaching: MAP_NovaGrid_v1.xlsx, SLA_Terms_NovaGrid.pdf, deployment_schedule.csv

Thanks — I’ll hold open calendar slots next week for a quick tie-off call.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@novagrid.com>

Cc: NovaGrid Procurement <procurement@novagrid.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Post-signature phased acceptance & evaluation tie-offs - NovaGrid

Ben —

Thanks, received. A couple of quick clarifying questions from procurement and engineering before we schedule the tie-off call: 

1) Procurement asks whether the SLA_Terms_NovaGrid.pdf is the final appended schedule for the contract or a placeholder. We need the final SLA language for our legal review by Nov 24.

2) From engineering: we prefer the canary criteria to include both system-level SLOs and a data-quality gate. Can you add a simple pass/fail checklist for the canonical prompts (we have 5 test prompts across core flows)? Also, please confirm whether KV/prefix-caching will be enabled in the private deployment (we will need guidance on cache warming).

3) On training: can you provide two separate sessions — one for our SREs (deep ops + metrics) and one for product/ops owners (operational runbook + rollback)?

We can do a call Nov 19 at 10:00 PT if that works. Procurement would also like an itemized acceptance artifact per canary wave to sign off.

—Elaine
Head of Platform Engineering, NovaGrid

-----Original Message-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@novagrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Post-signature phased acceptance & evaluation tie-offs - NovaGrid

Elaine —

Great questions. Short answers up front: SLA document attached to the MAP is the contracted schedule we will honor — Ben will send the redline-ready PDF. We can and should include a per-wave acceptance checklist; I sketched one into the MAP workbook under the "Acceptance Criteria" tab (attached). High-level technical commitments and notes: 

- Canary gating: we will run two discrete canary waves (10% then 50%). Each gate requires:
  - System health: no node OOMs, average GPU utilization < 85% for the pool, 99th-percentile request success rate >= 99.9%
  - Latency: p95 token-generation latency target < 450ms for the canonical prompt suite
  - Quality: automated regression eval on the 5 canonical prompts; allowed delta <= 2% for F1/rouge-like metric vs. baseline, plus manual spot checks (3 samples)
  - Data safety: no PII leakage detected in canary logs; we will run the redaction QA job after cache-warm

- Cache plan: yes, KV/prefix caching will be enabled by default for your private deployment. We recommend a 2-hour pre-warm window before each canary wave; script and warmup commands are in deployment_schedule.csv.

- Training: we will run two instructor-led 90-minute sessions: SRE ops deep-dive (runbooks, tracing, autoscaler knobs) and Product Ops (acceptance flow, rollback, user-facing behavior). Proposed dates: Nov 30 & Dec 2 (times in MAP).

Action items I own: finalize the acceptance checklist into a signoff sheet and provide the automated eval harness (link in MAP). Priyom will own the canary rollout automation and will be on the kickoff call for runbook signoff.

If Nov 19 10:00 PT works for you I’ll be on the call; otherwise share a slot.

—Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
